Subject: Dedicated capacity: Ellipse Labs workload details & commit/discount discussion

Hi Amit —

Thanks for the time last week. Attached is a quick profile template (Ellipse_Workload_Profile_2027-07.pdf) that will help us finalize the Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) recommendation. A few clarifying asks so we can lock a sizing + pricing recommendation: 

- Monthly request volume (total API calls) and distribution by endpoint (chat completion vs. embedding vs. rerank).
- Typical response size in tokens (median and 95th) and average user message length (you mentioned multi-turn chat with summaries).
- Expected concurrency and typical peak duration (e.g., sustained 10–15 min spikes or short bursts).
- Model mix you want served on Dedicated (e.g., mix of Llama2-70B-8bit for high-throughput vs. a 13B high-quality model).
- Any hard latency SLO (p50/p95) or throughput guarantees required for SLA.

Prelim thinking (very rough): given the scenarios you described in the demo (real-time chat, ~200–400 tokens per response, heavier bursts during product events) we expect a baseline pool of 3 x H100-80GB configured for high-concurrency serving with continuous batching would comfortably handle ~420 sustained rps for small-chat models and ~120 rps for 70B-class models with a mixed precision quantization profile. For a committed discount conversation, we typically size to the 75th percentile of sustained load and add burst headroom (20–30%).

If you can push back numbers this afternoon I’ll circulate a firm sizing + 12/24-month commit pricing table for procurement.

—Marissa

Hi Marissa —

Thanks — attaching the filled profile inline below and a quick summary: 

- Expected monthly API calls: ~9.2M (steady-state).
- Endpoint split: chat completion 72%, embeddings 18%, misc/rerank 10%.
- Average response size (chat): median 180 tokens, 95th ~560.
- Context + system prompts: typical context length ~2,048 tokens (occasionally up to 7,000 for long history retrieval flows).
- Concurrency: baseline 250 concurrent active sessions; predictable spikes to ~820 concurrent for 6–12 minutes during nightly batch windows and product notifications.
- Model mix: primary inference on a quantized 70B variant for user-facing chat (high quality), fallback to a 13B 8-bit model for lower-cost responses during peak.
- Latency goal: p95 < 900ms for 70B responses; p50 < 220ms.

Procurement note: we’re targeting a 12–month commitment with an option to scale month-to-month. Can we show a committed pricing band (0.5x / 1x / 2x baseline commits) and corresponding discount tiers? Also please flag if the 7k token contexts require a different pool configuration.

Thanks,
Amit
Amit Shah
Head of Product, Ellipse Labs
amit@ellipselabs.com

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: Ellipse Labs workload details & commit/discount discussion

Amit —

Great detail, thanks. Quick sizing notes and economics:

1) Contexts up to 7k tokens: these materially increase KV cache and memory pressure. For reliable p95 < 900ms on the 70B variant we recommend a mix:
   - Primary pool: 4 x H100-80GB (or 5 x A100-80GB equivalent) configured for 64 concurrent worker threads, kernel fusion enabled, and a 24GB KV cache allocation per GPU. This should hit ~350 rps for 70B under median token sizes and sustain bursts to ~700 rps with graceful queueing and autoscale buffers.

2) Cost-optimized fallback pool: 2 x A100-40GB for the 13B model to take 100–150 rps at lower cost during peaks; routing policy to spill non-critical requests after latency threshold.

3) Commit sizing bands (monthly reserved vGPU-equivalents):
   - 0.5x baseline: ~3 x H100 reserved — suitable if you accept higher spill-to-fallback during peaks — discount: 15% off list Dedicated rate.
   - 1x baseline: ~4 x H100 reserved — recommended minimum for your SLOs — discount: 22% off list.
   - 2x baseline: ~7 x H100 reserved — for heavy event-driven growth and sustained concurrency — discount: 30% with volume rebate at year-end.

We’ll send a line-item pricing workbook but rough delta: moving from 3→4 H100 is ~+28% committed monthly cost, while 4→7 adds ~+60% (but reduces spill and per-token overage by ~45% in our model).

Operational note: for the 7k context flows we suggest a two-tier policy: keep long-history retrieval and summarization off the low-latency path where possible (pre-summarize and store shorter context) to reduce peak KV cache usage.

Cheers,
Ben

Director, Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

Ben / Marissa —

This is helpful. A few procurement questions: 

- If we lock a 12-month 1x baseline commit (4x H100 reserved), can we get a 30-day rolling capacity buffer for product events (i.e., bursted hours that exceed reserved capacity) billed at a reduced overage rate rather than full list overage?
- Is a 99.9% uptime SLA and a p95 latency SLO for the reserved pool something Redwood will put in the contract with credits?
- Do you support model pinning & automatic fallback to the 13B pool at the routing layer (we want deterministic behavior during spikes)?

Procurement also asks for a simple three-column PDF that maps commit level → monthly charge → estimated cost per 1k tokens for our expected mix. Can you produce that and include a sample DocuSign term sheet?

Regards,
Amit

Amit —

Summary and next steps:

- Sizing: Redwood recommends 4 x H100-80GB primary + 2 x A100-40GB fallback for your stated profiles to meet p95 < 900ms for primary model and provide deterministic fallback during peaks.
- Commit options: we will prepare a 3-tier commit workbook (0.5x / 1x / 2x) with explicit monthly charges, per-1k-token economics for your chat-heavy mix, and a recommended overage buffer product (30-day rolling burst pool) priced at a discounted uplift to standard overage.
- SLA: Redwood can include a 99.9% uptime SLA for Dedicated with service credits; we'll surface the exact credit table in the term sheet.
- Model routing: yes — model pinning + deterministic fallback routing is supported; we'll include a suggested traffic policy config (canary %, fallback threshold latency).

Attachments: I’ve uploaded the term sheet draft and a sample pricing summary. Please review and send procurement questions; Ben will provide the workbook numbers by EOD tomorrow.

Proposed action items:
- Ben: produce commit workbook and token-cost mapping (EOD 2027-08-04).
- Neha: draft term sheet with SLA & overage buffer language (draft for internal review by 2027-08-05).
- Amit / Procurement: confirm which commit band you prefer (0.5x / 1x / 2x) so we can lock final pricing.

Thanks — talk soon.

—Marissa
